target.statement: K-SCAN achieves ARI > 0.99 on the 1M-point noisy Iris dataset with k'=1000 micro-clusters (Table 2, row k'=1000: ARI 0.9906, 3 clusters, 4.79% noise)
target.dataset: iris_1M_noise.csv (synthetic 1M-point KDE extension of UCI Iris with ~4.5% uniform noise)

compute.basis: No code or data released; must reimplement K-SCAN (MiniBatchKMeans + weighted DBSCAN + label propagation) and regenerate the 1M-point KDE-synthesized Iris dataset from the paper's description, then run on CPU; the paper itself reports ~13 s per run on 2 vCPU, so the dominant cost is writing/validating the reimplementation and data synthesis, not compute.

blockers: No code repository or link provided in the paper
iris_1M_noise.csv is not publicly released; must be regenerated via KDE from UCI Iris, and exact reproduction of the 0.9906 ARI depends on unspecified KDE bandwidth, noise sampling, and random seeds
Weighted DBSCAN details (sample_weight handling, MinPts=5000 semantics on 1000 centroids) are underspecified
title: The K-SCAN Clustering Algorithm
